clue.text: They may shoot, letting out a scream

indicators.note: letting something out, as with a garment's seams, loosens it, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone or something that may open fire while giving a loud yell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' suggests guns, but cameras shoot photographs and film. 'letting out' rearranges A SCREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers and film crews are said to shoot pictures, and these devices are what they shoot with.

clue.text: Mix the ingredients for porridge

parts.note: reads as a cooking instruction, but the verb for mixing a pan's contents is also British slang for prison, and porridge is British slang for time served

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, 'porridge' is a prison sentence (from the sitcom of that name), and the four-letter word for mixing is also slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to mix with a spoon, and as slang it means prison, where porridge (a jail term) is served.

clue.text: Runs into writer leading partnership agreement

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the writer word, placed within it

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
up means ahead or leading, as in a team being two goals up

explanation.surface: A scoring cricketer becomes an author who heads a business partnership deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenuptial contract is an agreement made by a couple before marriage, a partnership of a sort.

clue.text: Greek island — one suppressing a country no longer

indicators.note: in a down entry, pressing down on something means sitting above it, so the one letter comes on top of the a

parts.note: Rhodes is a large island of the Dodecanese in Greece
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Greek island is said to be holding down some nation that has ceased to exist.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former name of the African state now called Zimbabwe, so it is a nation that no longer exists.

clue.text: Arrange loan with choirs performing at the same time

indicators.note: choirs performing are put through their paces in a fresh shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so the letters of loan are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An organiser fixes a loan so that choirs can sing together in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams side by side: 'performing' turns CHOIRS into ISOCHR, and 'Arrange' turns LOAN into ONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things happening at equal time intervals or simultaneously, from Greek roots for equal and time.

clue.text: Former police station is the cause of all evil

parts.note: old can mean former, as in an old boss
nick is British slang for a police station

explanation.surface: A disused police station is blamed as the source of every wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for a police station (or prison).
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional nickname for the Devil, the figure seen as the source of all wickedness.

clue.text: Cross when back legs start to get weary

indicators.note: back tells us the word for when is read from right to left

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the start of legs is its opening letter

parts.note: to tire is to become weary

explanation.surface: Someone grows irritable when their legs begin to feel worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross in heraldry, as on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Order new titles with hope at first

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of hope

explanation.surface: An instruction to issue fresh titles, beginning with an optimistic one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but it is the definition: the Order of the Thistle is a Scottish order of chivalry. 'new' rearranges TITLES with H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of chivalry, often called simply by the plant's name.

clue.text: Gossip hasn't ruined stroke

indicators.note: ruined means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Idle chatter has not spoiled someone's caress.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis this is a shot hit past an opponent at the net, one kind of stroke.

clue.text: Help required to follow trial?

indicators.note: the help word comes after the trial word

parts.note: a hearing is a court trial or inquiry
aid means help

explanation.surface: Assistance needed by someone trying to keep up with a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the device: help needed to follow (hear) what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: This device helps people with poor hearing follow conversations, so it is help needed to follow speech.

clue.text: Unable to pitch?

definitions.meaning: a contraction of cannot, meaning unable
a slope or tilt, as in the pitch of a roof

explanation.definitionFit: Read with an apostrophe it means cannot; without one it means a tilt or slope, a pitch.

clue.text: Instruments played by smoker wearing trousers?

indicators.note: the trousers word is worn around the smoker word, which goes inside it

parts.note: bags is old British slang for loose trousers
a pipe is something one smokes

explanation.surface: Musical instruments played by a person who smokes and wears trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old British slang for baggy trousers, as in Oxford bags.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish wind instrument is played by squeezing a bag that feeds air into reed pipes.

clue.text: Where children might enjoy quiet wager on good game of golf?

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, quietly
to lay a bet is to wager
a round is a complete game of golf

explanation.surface: Kids might like a quiet bet on a decent round on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: A play area at a school or park is a place set aside for children to have fun.

clue.text: Impressed drivers finally in front of commercial vehicle

indicators.note: the drivers letter comes before the vehicle word
finally takes the closing letter of drivers

parts.note: a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Motorists were impressed at last by a lorry ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To be struck by something is to be impressed by it.

clue.text: Andrew perhaps is not partisan in dispute

indicators.note: in dispute suggests the letters are at odds and scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Andrew is neutral in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrew is the protecting saint of Scotland, an example of this kind of figure.

clue.text: Calmly submissive, offered to leave

definitions.meaning: accepting what cannot be changed without complaint
having given up one's job by notice

explanation.definitionFit: The word means meekly accepting one's fate and also having handed in one's notice.

clue.text: Off supporting Triumph plant?

indicators.note: in a down entry the off word sits underneath the car, holding it up

parts.note: Triumph was a British car make
away means off, as in gone

explanation.surface: Someone going off in support of victory, possibly as a factory?
explanation.walkthrough: Triumph was a British car manufacturer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an umbrella-flowered herb whose seeds are used as a spice, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Went in bearing tender for exchange

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: for exchange means the letters of tender are swapped about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone went inside carrying money to swap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' suggests money, but it is the anagram fodder; 'for exchange' gives NTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go in, so the past tense means went in.

clue.text: Burns food for 20?

parts.note: looks like burning a meal for twenty guests, but means the dish celebrated by poet Robert Burns, national food of the answer at 20 across

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, wrote an address to this dish; 20 across is SCOTLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns Night suppers serve this Scottish pudding of offal and oats, Scotland's national dish.

clue.text: Bed left in smooth state once

indicators.note: the bed and left letters go in the smooth word

parts.note: to sand is to smooth
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A bed abandoned in some formerly flat country.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an independent kingdom until union with England in 1707, so a state once.

clue.text: Food that may be caught in cowboy's territory

indicators.note: caught in means the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something to eat that might be lassoed on a cowboy's land.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellfish is eaten raw or cooked, so it is a food.

clue.text: Food like this has a good filling

indicators.note: the answer is the filling inside the words has a good, sitting across them

explanation.surface: A dish of this kind has a nice filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pie with a nice filling, but the food sits inside 'has a good', and 'filling' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: This starch from palm pith is cooked into puddings, so it is a food.

clue.text: Polish and sign lists of technical terms

parts.note: gloss means shine or polish
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An instruction to polish and sign some reference lists.
explanation.definitionFit: These are alphabetical word lists explaining specialised vocabulary.

clue.text: Overwhelming victory right away?

parts.note: out means away, as in not at home

explanation.surface: Is a crushing win absolutely beyond doubt?
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a decisive defeat for the losers, an overwhelming win for the victors.

clue.text: Sounded exhausted around lunchtime, and put a coat on

indicators.note: the exhausted word goes around the lunchtime letter

parts.note: panted means breathed hard, sounding exhausted
one o'clock is lunchtime, and I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone was breathing heavily at noon and pulled on a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint something is to cover it with a coat of paint.

clue.text: Bewildered, finding inspiration in place of rest

indicators.note: the inspiration word goes in the place of rest

parts.note: a bed is where one rests
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: A puzzled person found creative ideas while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means puzzled or confused, the same as bewildered.
